intro.en: Words for maybe. The expression and the speaker's degree of certainty influence the mood.

quizá.nota: Also written quizás; pronunciation varies between seseo and distinción.

puede que.nota: In this possibility pattern, use the subjunctive: puede que venga.

igual.nota: Colloquial in Spain, with the indicative.

texto.en:
These expressions normally use the indicative: **a lo mejor**, **igual** (colloquial in Spain), **seguro que**, **supongo que**.

- **A lo mejor** me **quedo** en casa.

Expressions such as **puede (ser) que**, **es posible que** and **es probable que** use the subjunctive: **Puede que nieve**.

With **quizá(s)** and **tal vez**, either mood is possible: **Quizá viene / venga** mañana. **Probablemente**, **posiblemente** and **seguramente** can also take the indicative or present subjunctive: **Seguramente está / esté** en casa. The speaker's degree of certainty can influence the choice, but context and regional usage also matter.

When **no sé si** means ‘I don't know whether’, the indicative is usual in Spain and many other varieties: **No sé si viene** mañana. Some varieties, including Mexican, Caribbean and Andean Spanish, also use the subjunctive here. The accent distinguishes **si** (‘whether’) from **sí** (‘yes’).

frases.en: Are you coming to the mountains on Saturday?

frases.es: No sé si puedo. Quizá tenga que trabajar.
frases.en: I don't know if I can. I may have to work.

frases.es: Puede que nieve. Es probable que haga mucho frío.
frases.en: It may snow. It's likely to be very cold.

frases.es: Entonces a lo mejor me quedo en casa.
frases.en: Then maybe I'll stay at home.
I'm sure you'll come in the end.

llueva.en: In this possibility pattern, use the subjunctive.

lloverá.en: Use the subjunctive with puede que: llueva.

pregunta.en: Complete: maybe I'll stay at home.

bloques.frase: A lo mejor me ___ en casa.

quedo.en: A lo mejor normally uses the indicative: me quedo.

quede.en: The usual pattern after a lo mejor is indicative: me quedo.

quedar.en: The subject is yo, so use the conjugated present me quedo.

pregunta.en: Complete: I don't know if he is coming.

viene.en: The indicative is the usual neutral choice here; some varieties also use the subjunctive.

venga.en: The indicative is the usual neutral choice here; some varieties also use the subjunctive.

venir.en: Venir would mean whether I should come.

pregunta.en: Which one can take either mood?

tal vez.en: Tal vez viene and tal vez venga are both possible.

bloques.frase: Quizá tenga que trabajar el sábado

traduccion.en: I may have to work on Saturday.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about your plans for the summer when nothing is certain yet: quizá, a lo mejor, puede que, es probable que.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Speculate aloud about what you will be doing in five years.
